subtopics.name: Impact of Errors on Profit & Financial Position

parts.problem_md:
On 31 December 2023 Jean identified the following errors. - A purchase of stationery for office use, \$30, had been entered in the purchases account. - The sales account had been undercast by \$200 - A cheque, \$300, received from J Arthur had been credited to the account of J Alfred. - A credit sale to Jones, \$78, had been correctly entered in the sales account but debited to Jones’ account as \$87 Prepare journal entries to correct these errors. Narratives are **not **required. **Journal** | 2023 | Details | Debit
\$ | Credit
\$ | |---|---|---|---| | 31 December | | | | | | | | | | 31 December | | | | | | | | | | 31 December | | | | | | | | | | 31 December | | | |
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]** > **Award marks as indicated for correct details and amounts.** > > **Journal** > > | 2023 | Details | Debit
\$ | Credit
\$ | > |---|---|---|---| > | 31 December | Stationery | 30 **(1)** | | > | | Purchases | | 30** (1)** | > | 31 December | Suspense | 200** (1)** | | > | | Sales | | 200 **(1)** | > | 31 December | J Alfred | 300** (1)** | | > | | J Arthur | | 300** (1)** | > | 31 December | Suspense | 9** (1)** | | > | | Jones | | 9 **(1)** |

parts.problem_md:
On 31 August 2023 Jones, a sole trader, identified the following errors and omissions. 1. A withdrawal of cash for personal use, \$650, had not been recorded. 2. A payment for motor expenses, \$234, had been posted to the motor vehicles account. 3. A cheque paid for general expenses, \$65, had been entered in the cash book as \$56 Prepare journal entries to record the correction of **each **of these errors and omissions. Narratives are not required. | | Account | Debit
\$ | Credit
\$ | |---|---|---|---| | August 31 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]** > **Award 1 mark for correct figures with account names.** > > | | Account | Debit
\$ | Credit
\$ | > |---|---|---|---| > | August 31 | Drawings | 650** (1)** | | > | | Cash | | 650 **(1)** | > | | Motor expenses | 234 **(1)** | | > | | Motor vehicles | | 234 **(1)** | > | | General expenses | 9** (1)** | | > | | Bank | | 9 **(1)** |

parts.problem_md: State which account is opened when a trial balance does not balance.

> **Award mark as indicated.**

parts.problem_md:
State the type of error in each scenario.

| Scenario | Type of error |
|---|---|
| Cash drawings of \$175 had not been recorded. |   |
| Wages of \$180 had been recorded in the cash book as \$80 |   |
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Award marks as indicated.**
> 
> | Scenario | Type of error |
> |---|---|
> | Cash drawings of \$175 had not been recorded. | Omission **(1)** |
> | Wages of \$180 had been recorded in the cash book as \$80 | Original entry **(1)** |

parts.problem_md:
Explain the effect on owner’s equity of:

(i) **not **recording cash drawings of \$175

(2)

(ii) recording wages as \$80 instead of \$180

(2)
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> (i) **Award 1 mark for each valid point up to a maximum of 2 marks. **
> 
> **Sample answer **
> 
> Owner’s equity would be overstated **(1) **as cash drawings reduce owner’s equity **(1)**.
> 
> **Accept any other appropriate responses.**
> 
> (ii)** Award 1 mark for each valid point up to a maximum of 2 marks. **
> 
> **Sample answer**
> 
> Owner’s equity would be overstated **(1)** as expenses were understated **(1).**
> 
> **Accept any other appropriate responses.**

parts.problem_md:
Returns inwards, \$150, was posted to the credit of returns outwards.

Identify how this transaction would be corrected in the books of account.

|   | Account to be debited | Account to be credited |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | Returns inwards \$150 Returns outwards \$150 | Suspense account \$300 |
| **B** | Suspense account \$300 | Returns inwards \$150 Returns outwards \$150 |
| **C** | Returns inwards \$150 | Suspense account \$150 |
| **D** | Returns outwards \$150 | Suspense account \$150 |
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> |   | Account to be debited | Account to be credited |
> |---|---|---|
> | **A** | Returns inwards \$150 Returns outwards \$150 | Suspense account \$300 |

parts.problem_md: State **one **difference between an error of **commission** and an error of **principle**.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Award marks as indicated. **
> 
> An error of commission is where the transaction is entered in an incorrect account of the** same class (1) **whereas an error of principle occurs when the transaction is entered in the **wrong class** of account** (1)**
> 
> **Accept any other appropriate responses.**

parts.problem_md: State **one **other type of error that does **not** affect the balancing of the trial balance.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Award mark as indicated. Max 1 mark.**
> 
> - Omission** (1) **
> - Complete reversal** (1) **
> - Compensating **(1) **
> - Original entry** (1) **
> - Transposition **(1)**

parts.problem_md: Identify the type of error when a sales invoice for \$500 is entered in the sales day book as \$450.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> **The correct answer is C** (Original entry)

parts.problem_md:
At the end of his financial year, 31 March 2021, Jacques prepared a trial balance and opened a suspense account with a debit balance of \$210

Jacques has found the following errors.

1. Motor insurance, \$400, had been posted to the debit side of the motor vehicles account.
2. A cheque received from a credit customer, \$650, had been entered correctly in the cash book but had been entered as \$560 on the credit side of the customer’s account.
3. A direct debit, \$120, for general expenses had not been entered.
4. Returns inwards, \$150, had been posted to the credit side of the returns outwards account.

State the type of error made in error 1.
parts.solution_md:
> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Award marks as indicated.**
> 
> Principle** (1).**
